answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a nebula as the anchor of the cost.
